name: Turkish Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language; no published description of word stress found (word stress not applicable in the spoken-language sense)

sources.citation: Kelepir, Meltem (ed.). 2020. A Grammar of Turkish Sign Language (TİD). 1st ed. (SIGN-HUB Sign Language Grammar Series). 418 pp. Open access, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Part 2 Phonology, Chapter 2 'Prosody' (author: Kadir Gökgöz), PDF pp. 77-88.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress/accent position stated. Sec. 2.1.2 Foot (PDF p. 82): 'In this level, syllables are organized into rhythmically strong and weak syllables. A foot is a rhythmic unit and it is made up of one or two syllables' -- which syllable is strong is never specified. Sec. 2.2.1 Prosodic word is defined by non-manual domain markers (mouthing/mouth gesture, head position) and cliticization, not by prominence. The word 'stress' occurs only in a glossary definition of 'syllable' and in an English-translation remark on focus.

sources.citation: Kubuş, Okan. 2008. An analysis of Turkish Sign Language (TİD) phonology and morphology. MA thesis, Middle East Technical University (Graduate School of Informatics, Cognitive Science), Ankara. xviii+174 pp.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or prominence; phonology chapter covers handshape, location, movement, Hand-Tier and Brentari Prosodic Model representations, minimal pairs, phonological processes. Conclusion notes prosody of TİD 'need[s] further research'.
